status: NOT AUTHORITATIVE — do not code against this file
whatThisWas: An early (2024) design sketch for a nested-tree JSON model of the Thai codes. It was never implemented that way and it does NOT describe the live data. It also mislabels 'constitution' (that key is พระธรรมนูญศาลยุติธรรม, not a constitution).

corpus.shape: books.<collectionKey>.articles.<number> -> { id, number, text, cancelled, meta, keywords, caseLaw, examples, lectureNotes?, examFreq? }. meta is a FLAT structural descriptor { phaak/phaakTitle, laksana/laksanaTitle, muad/muadTitle, suan/suanTitle } — NOT a nested tree. Multi-instrument collections key articles as '<instrumentId>::<number>'.
corpus.note: This remains the source corpus and is not migrated.

ontology.role: Authoritative per-collection configuration: native structural levels + their Thai labels, provision unit, instrument model, subject area, source attribution, patch flags. Add or reshape a collection HERE.

api.role: The shared navigation/information layer. listSubjectAreas · listCollections · getCollection · getInstrument · getStructureTree · resolveProvision · getBreadcrumb · describePath · getAdjacent · resolveAtlasId · makeAtlasId · compareNumbers. Do not reimplement these per page.

ui.role: Registry-driven navigation UI structure (Subject Area -> Collection -> Instrument -> native hierarchy -> Provision). Host page: atlas.html.

identityScheme.legacyId: <collection>_<number>  (frozen — every existing link, GA4, SEO uses this). Multi-instrument: <collection>_<instrument>::<number>
identityScheme.principle: ONE ATLAS, MULTIPLE LEGAL ONTOLOGIES — collection-native hierarchy is preserved, not flattened into a universal Code->Book->Title->Chapter->Section model.
